newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CAPTALL PLANS NEW BANKING ACQUISITION SOON.
newsitem.headline: CAPTALL PLANS NEW BANKING ACQUISITION SOON.

text.p: South Africa's Capital Alliance Holdings said on Wednesday it would continue along the successful acquisition trail it had set and would soon announce an acquisition in the country's personal banking sector.

"Personal banking, whatever you want to call it, we should shortly be announcing a deal on an acquisition there. The deal will probably be sealed tomorrow," chief executive Mark Barnes told an investment analysts presentation.

Captall -- part of the black empowerment group that bought control of mining house JCI Ltd earlier this year -- said it planned to be one of South Africa's top five financial services groups within seven to 10 years.
"We aim to be one of the top five financial services groups in South Africa within the next seven to 10 years. But, frankly, I'll be surprised if it takes us that long," said Barnes.

"We want to build a broadly-based, truly South African financial services group, creating shareholder wealth through sustained earnings growth and capital investment," he told an investment analysts presentation in Johannesburg.
Acquisitions would form part of the group's strategy to expand, as they have done in the past.
"We do have an acquisition profile. It's part of our daily job description. We aim for a disciplined process of methodically and scientifically pursuing acquisition opportunities," Barnes said.
The group said that acquisitions were behind its surge in earnings for the 12 months to end-March.
Last month Captall announced earnings per share of 102.4 cents before exceptional items compared to 52.9 cents a year ago. It increased its dividend to 15 cents from 10 cents.
Barnes put the spotlight on the group's Capital Alliance Bank, formerly NDH Bank Ltd and acquired by Captall in the last financial year.
He said the bank aimed to broaden its relationship interface to develop a fully-fledged merchant bank within 18 months.

This would involve developing a personal financial advice business -- the reasoning behind the planned acquisition -- as well as developing its investment banking business. "We have about eight live deals at the moment," Barnes said.
Captall expected "huge" growth in its asset management division which currently has assets under management worth more than 1.2 billion rand.
"I'd be very surprised if we didn't quadruple this in a very short time, meaning a few months," Barnes said, adding that this was one area where Captall could seek a foreign alliance.
Capital Alliance Life was also looking at acquisitions. "We're going to focus outward. We are very focused on acquisitions," Barnes said.
Capital Alliance Life increased its total premium income in the last financial year to 274 million rand from 139 million.
Barnes said the group had an aspirant client base and planned to be a low cost producer in the industry.

Captall's growth strategy would also entail the group using its strong capital base -- in excess of 1.2 billion rand -- rather than storing it, building operating earnings and using the synergies afforded it by its various operations.
